newsitem.title: FRANCE: Popularity of Chirac and Juppe falls again.
newsitem.headline: Popularity of Chirac and Juppe falls again.

text.p: The popularity of French President Jacques Chirac and of Prime Minister Alain Juppe is falling again with only about a third of voters expressing confidence in their action, an opinion poll showed on Wednesday.
The poll for the Catholic weekly La Vie showed 36 percent had confidence in Chirac and 30 percent in Juppe, down three percent and two percent on last month.
The number of people who said they lacked confidence in the two was 55 percent and 61 percent respectively, up six points and five points.

The popularity of the two men, who came to power after Chirac's election in May 1995, started falling at the end of the same year amid a crippling nationwide transport strike and only began slowly rising again recently.
Previous surveys had shown Chirac's and Juppe's popularity picking up slighly in recent weeks amid controversy over a law tightening controls on illegal immigrants.

The latest poll, conducted on March 27 by the CSA Institute among 1,010 people, comes exactly a year before key general elections which could see Chirac having to "co-habit" with a left-wing opposition-led parliament.
